indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER] presenting with back pain and failure to emit stool for four days. Evaluate for bowel obstruction versus other etiologies.
technique: ** Axial CT images were acquired from the diaphragm to the pubic symphysis following the administration of intravenous contrast. Multiplanar reformations were performed.
findings:
**
The liver demonstrates a smooth contour and normal attenuation without focal mass lesions. The gallbladder is present without wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. The biliary tree is not dilated. The spleen and pancreas are unremarkable in size and enhancement pattern. The adrenal glands are symmetric and within normal limits. The kidneys show symmetric excretion of contrast without evidence of hydronephrosis or nephrolithiasis.
Regarding the gastrointestinal tract, there is no evidence of high-grade mechanical bowel obstruction. There is mild, non-specific dilation of the colon with fecal loading throughout the descending and sigmoid colon, consistent with constipation. The stomach and small bowel loops are normal in caliber. There is no free intraperitoneal air or abnormal fluid collection identified.
The urinary bladder is partially filled and appears unremarkable. The pelvic organs are unremarkable for the patient's age, showing expected involutional changes.
Evaluation of the visualized skeleton reveals a significant destructive osseous lesion involving the T12 vertebral body. There is extensive cortical destruction and loss of vertebral height resulting in an acute collapse of the T12 body. The posterior elements are partially involved. There is no evidence of significant retropulsion into the spinal canal or associated epidural hematoma. Mild degenerative spondylosis is noted throughout the lumbar spine with small marginal osteophytes at L3 and L4. There is also mild atherosclerotic calcification of the abdominal aorta.
conclusion:
**
Destructive bony metastasis in the T12 vertebra with associated vertebral body collapse; no evidence of spinal canal compromise.
